trip_summary: A 4-night Lisbon stay focused on neighborhoods, coastal walks, and local tascas, prioritizing authentic food experiences and Atlantic views while staying well under budget.

key_decisions.decision: Stay in Graça or Alfama rather than Baixa/Chiado
key_decisions.reasoning: More local character, cheaper accommodation (roughly €40-50/night vs €70+), proximity to authentic restaurants without Rossio Square tourist markup
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Central Baixa for convenience, but contradicts 'avoiding tourist traps' preference

key_decisions.decision: Dedicate one full day to Cascais/Guincho coastline via train
key_decisions.reasoning: Coastline is a stated interest; train is cheap (typically €2-3 each way) and the clifftop paths deliver Atlantic drama without organized tour pricing
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Sintra, but coastline matches interests more directly and is less crowded

key_decisions.reasoning: Entry fees eat budget (€12-15 combined), crowds contradict pace preference, and exterior views plus waterfront parks are free
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Classic 'must-see' but misaligned with anti-tourist-trap stance

key_decisions.decision: Prioritize tascas and neighborhood mercados over sit-down restaurants for most meals
key_decisions.reasoning: Vegetarian petiscos (small plates) and market counters deliver local authenticity at €6-10/meal vs €15-25 for full restaurant service
key_decisions.alternative_considered: One nicer dinner, but budget is tight and request emphasizes 'local food' not fine dining

key_decisions.decision: Walk everywhere except Cascais day trip
key_decisions.reasoning: Lisbon is compact for core neighborhoods; metro/tram costs add up (€1.50+ per ride), walking reveals street life and keeps transport under €10 total
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Tram 28 for experience, but it's a tourist magnet and walking is free

items.title: Arrival and metro to accommodation
items.reasoning: Metro is cheaper than taxi (roughly €1.50 vs €15+); arrival timing assumes afternoon flight typical for short-haul EU

items.title: Check-in to guesthouse/hostel private room
items.reasoning: 4 nights at roughly €45/night keeps lodging to 36% of budget; Graça is residential with miradouros and local density

items.title: Walk Graça to Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
items.reasoning: Sunset viewpoint, free, establishes bearings on Day 1 without strain

items.title: Dinner at neighborhood tasca
items.reasoning: Vegetable-heavy petiscos (grilled peppers, fava stew, tortilla) at local spot; first meal sets 'avoid tourist traps' tone

items.title: Walk Alfama to Portas do Sol, explore lanes
items.reasoning: Adjacent to Graça, pre-tourist-hour timing, labyrinthine streets reveal tile facades and neighborhood rhythms

items.title: Coffee and pastel de nata at local café
items.reasoning: Icon food but sourced locally, not from Belém factory line; roughly €1 pastry + €1.50 coffee

items.title: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
items.reasoning: Walk or short metro; neighborhood market hall less touristy than Timeout/Ribeira, browse stalls

items.title: Lunch at market counter (vegetarian option)
items.reasoning: Vegetable plate or soup + small bite at market pricing

items.title: Walk Jardim da Estrela to riverfront
items.reasoning: Relaxed pace, green space to waterfront, observe local family life in park

items.title: Dinner at traditional cervejaria
items.reasoning: Grilled vegetables, salad, bread; cervejarias offer sit-down atmosphere without fine-dining cost

days.feasibility_flag: 6 activities/meals scheduled in one day — likely overpacked, review pacing.

items.title: Train to Cascais
items.reasoning: Coastal line, roughly €2.30 each way; early start maximizes daylight for coastline walking

items.title: Walk Cascais to Guincho beach via Boca do Inferno
items.reasoning: Clifftop path, dramatic Atlantic views, roughly 6km one-way but relaxed pace allows for breaks; core coastline interest

items.title: Picnic lunch from Cascais market
items.reasoning: Bread, cheese, fruit bought pre-walk; budget-friendly and fits beach setting

items.title: Guincho beach walk and return bus to Cascais
items.reasoning: Wide Atlantic beach, surf vibe; bus back (roughly €2) rather than 6km return walk conserves energy

items.title: Train return to Lisbon
items.reasoning: Included in morning estimate (round-trip)

items.title: Light dinner near accommodation
items.reasoning: After full day, simple neighborhood meal (soup, salad, small plate)

items.title: Walk to LX Factory
items.reasoning: Repurposed industrial zone, creative shops/cafés; touristy but less trap-like than Baixa, and walk along river is pleasant

items.title: Coffee at LX Factory café
items.reasoning: Specialty coffee culture here; one indulgence aligns with interests in local scenes

items.title: Belém waterfront walk (exterior views only)
items.reasoning: Adjacent to LX, Monument to Discoveries and Torre visible from gardens; skip interior queues and fees per earlier decision

items.title: Lunch at neighborhood spot in Ajuda
items.reasoning: Residential area uphill from Belém, cheaper than waterfront; vegetarian prato do dia (daily plate) typically available

items.title: Return walk via riverside to Cais do Sodré
items.reasoning: Roughly 5km, flat riverfront path, relaxed pace fits; golden hour along Tagus

items.title: Dinner at Bairro Alto tasca
items.reasoning: Final evening, slight step up in atmosphere but still local pricing; vegetarian options common in this zone

things_to_skip.item: Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower interiors
things_to_skip.reasoning: Entry fees (roughly €12-15 combined) consume 3% of total budget for queue-heavy monuments; exterior views deliver architectural impact without cost or crowds
Iconic but pickpocket-prone tourist magnet; same neighborhoods accessible on foot with more control over pace and route
Transport (€5 round-trip) plus palace entries (€15-30) and food inflates costs; coastline at Cascais better matches stated interests and budget
Curated food hall is upmarket tourist concept; Campo de Ourique and neighborhood tascas offer more authentic local eating at lower cost
Cover charges (€15-25) and minimum consumption requirements stress budget; street fado occasionally audible for free in evening walks
